question: Should OpenClaw reserve the top-level `auth` CLI root even though installed plugins can currently own that root?
rationale: The code cannot preserve both the proposed built-in alias and the current plugin root contract without an explicit namespace or precedence decision.

options.title: Keep the canonical command
options.body: Decline the top-level alias and retain `openclaw models auth list`, preserving existing plugin-owned command roots.

options.title: Reserve `auth` with migration
options.body: Approve the root only with a plugin namespace audit, deprecation or migration policy, collision tests, and upgrade documentation.

options.title: Design a composable auth root
options.body: Create an explicit core/plugin subcommand composition contract before adding `auth list`, rather than silently shadowing a plugin root.

recommendation.title: Keep the canonical command
recommendation.body: Decline the top-level alias and retain `openclaw models auth list`, preserving existing plugin-owned command roots.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent model-auth listing history and direct PR timeline interest make this the strongest available owner for the CLI/auth direction choice.
